title: E5 reading checkpoint form B
instructions: Use an eighteen-minute rehearsal target: survey both passages, complete one passage before moving to the other, park an uncertain item after one focused attempt, and protect time to answer all five questions before submitting.

parts.prompt: Passage A: In paragraph 2, who does “It” in “It repeated the riverside count” refer to?

choice_rationales.A: The concert created unusual traffic but did not conduct the survey.
choice_rationales.B: The cycling group made the decision and is the singular organisation able to repeat the count.
choice_rationales.C: Traffic is what the volunteers observe, not the observer.
choice_rationales.D: A location cannot repeat a count.

parts.hint: Protected checkpoint: no hint is available.
parts.correct_explanation: “It” refers to the youth cycling group that organised and repeated the survey.

parts.prompt: Passage A: What does “modest” most nearly mean in the final paragraph?

choice_rationales.A: The one-week lending trial is useful but too small to prove permanent change.
choice_rationales.B: The group reports the trial and its limits openly.
choice_rationales.C: The next clause rejects a permanent conclusion.

parts.hint: Protected checkpoint: no hint is available.
parts.correct_explanation: Modest means small or limited in size and ambition.

parts.prompt: Passage B: In the final paragraph, what does “it” in “I still turned it towards the street” refer to?

choice_rationales.A: The narrator contrasts the large sign with the object turned each evening.
choice_rationales.B: The rider uses the bakery telephone once; it is not placed in the window.
choice_rationales.C: The recurring task is to turn the small lamp towards the street.
choice_rationales.D: The shutters are closed during the power cut but are not described as being turned.

parts.hint: Protected checkpoint: no hint is available.
parts.correct_explanation: “It” refers to the small lamp in the bakery window.

parts.prompt: Passage B: What does “faint” most nearly mean in the opening paragraph?

choice_rationales.A: The lamp's weak glow is contrasted with the bright electric sign.
choice_rationales.C: The father checks the wick, but no repair is described.
choice_rationales.D: The delivery rider sees the lamp from the street.

parts.hint: Protected checkpoint: no hint is available.
parts.correct_explanation: Faint means giving little light or being difficult to see clearly.

parts.prompt: How do the two passages differ in the conclusion they draw from limited evidence?

options.text: Passage A recommends further measurement before claiming lasting change, while Passage B uses one event to revise a personal understanding.
Passage A makes a permanent policy claim, while Passage B refuses to interpret the power cut.
Both passages prove that one short trial always predicts future behaviour.
Both passages conclude that brighter lights are unnecessary after sunset.

choice_rationales.A: The cycling group preserves a research boundary, whereas the narrator draws a bounded personal lesson from the lamp helping one rider.
choice_rationales.B: Passage A explicitly avoids a permanent claim, and Passage B interprets the event carefully.
choice_rationales.C: The cycling group states that a longer programme and later count are needed.
choice_rationales.D: Both passages show that visibility matters; neither dismisses brighter lights.

parts.hint: Protected checkpoint: no hint is available.
parts.correct_explanation: The informational passage calls for follow-up evidence, while the reflective passage uses a single experience to change the narrator's own view without making a general scientific claim.
